record.title: China's national AI cybersecurity test reports 32 strong-performing teams across eight scenarios
record.summary: China's official result notice says a national AI-enabled cybersecurity application test drew 251 teams from 151 organizations across eight scenarios, with 32 teams described as achieving good results. The CAC release names teams by scenario but gives no scores or thresholds. CNCERT's earlier notice describes two stages and says the top six teams per scenario advanced to in-person testing; the organizer also restricted public sharing of detailed test materials and results without permission.
organizations: Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission of China
National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team/Coordination Center of China (CNCERT)

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: CNCERT announced a 2026 AI-enabled cybersecurity application test with eight scenarios, followed by the CAC-hosted publication of its results on 2026-09-15.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The CAC release reports 151 participating organizations and 251 teams, and says 32 teams achieved “good results,” listing teams by scenario. It does not publish scores or thresholds.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The CNCERT notice described online testing from 2026-06-07 to 2026-07-06, advancing the top six teams in each scenario to an in-person second stage from 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-15; the last submitted result determined the score.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The public result notice names teams but gives no team-level scores, thresholds, benchmark construction or measured performance; the original notice restricts public sharing of test materials and detailed process/results without organizer permission.

evidence_gaps.description: Public scores, thresholds, test construction, and team-level measurement are not present in the result notice; detailed test materials are subject to organizer restrictions.
The announcement provides no independent validation or deployment outcomes for the listed teams.

brief.importance_rationale: If the official account reflects the test process, this is a substantial national AI-cybersecurity evaluation program: 251 teams from 151 organizations entered eight scenarios and 32 were publicly named as strong performers, with results intended to inform sector adoption. The public release gives no scores, thresholds or technical protocol, so it does not establish comparative product capability or deployment readiness.
limitations: The CAC result notice reports the organizer’s qualitative “good results” assessment; it does not publish scores, thresholds, model identities for every team, or uncertainty.

The test’s detailed scenario specifications and test materials were not accessible in this review; the public CNCERT notice says detailed test data and results may not be shared without organizer permission.
No independent evaluation or post-deployment outcome was inspected; listed teams should not be interpreted as independently validated winners or as evidence of fielded capability.

technical.claimed_result: Official release reports 32 teams achieved “good results” across eight scenarios; no quantitative performance claim is supported.
technical.demonstrated_result: Official notices document a two-stage national AI cybersecurity test, its scenarios and participant counts, and publication of a qualitative result list.
technical.implementation_status: The test was completed and the organizer published a qualitative results list. Subsequent adoption and measured security effects are unknown.
technical.mechanism: CNCERT organized an eight-scenario evaluation. Its public May notice says the top six teams in each scenario advanced from online testing to an in-person second stage; public result materials identify teams but not scores.
technical.novelty: A new public result announcement from a multi-agency Chinese national AI cybersecurity test spanning eight application areas and naming teams qualitatively assessed as strong.
technical.regime: China’s 2026 national AI-enabled cybersecurity application test, conducted online and then in-person from June through August, with results announced September 14 and published by CAC September 15.
technical.reproducibility: Not reproducible from the public result announcement: team-level scores, thresholds, task construction and detailed scenario materials are not available in the inspected sources.
technical.strongest_baseline: No public benchmark baseline or comparable independent test results were supplied.

brief.title: China's national AI cybersecurity test reports 32 strong-performing teams across eight scenarios
brief.why_it_matters: The program is a sizable official effort to evaluate AI applications across cyber defense, vulnerability discovery, threat detection, AI safety and agent behavior, with results intended to inform sector adoption. Publicly available evidence establishes the test design and the organizer’s qualitative shortlist, not comparative accuracy, robustness or deployment readiness.
